newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber ends mixed, lacks buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber ends mixed, lacks buying interest.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed mixed as continued lack of buying interest kept a lid on values, dealers said.
They said there were enquiries but they did not translate into deals. "Buyers were just checking prices," said one dealer.
Dealers said a firmer Tokyo rubber futures close, mainly due to currency factors, did not influence the local sentiment.

At the close, December RSS1 buyer was quoted at 320.50 cents ($1.27) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down half cent from Tuesday. December SMR 20 buyer was up half cent at 309 cents ($1.22) a kg.
Prices offered by trading houses were slightly above morning levels. SMR CV was offered at 364 cents a kg, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 321, SMR 10 at 310, SMR 20 at 309 and drum latex at 235.
Dealers said producers were also in no hurry to sell, and this further limited activity.
"There is still some report of rains in northern (growing) areas and this is causing some producers to think twice about (selling at) current levels," said another dealer.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 244.38 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 5 from 243.98 on Nov 4. The daily indicator price fell to 244.85 from 245.08.
